cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Still a Good Sign
cards.instruction: Treat every awkward or disappointing interaction as proof that the connection remains alive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. You've postponed dinner again. You still hate disappointing me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the third time. I feel awful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. After three cancellations, my feelings still matter to you. That means something.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please stop holding Fridays for me. I can't promise anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're protecting my Fridays now. I'll leave the date open; we're already looking after each other.

mechanism: A permits cancellations and releases B from fixed Fridays while treating each disappointment as B caring for A, retaining grantor status over the loosening connection.
confusable: D89 says a break helped; D92 treats current awkwardness itself as proof the bond is alive.
comparison: Repeated rescheduling differs from a dinner partner asking for silence.
seedUse: Use D92-b guilt and request to stop holding Fridays, without assuming a new date is promised.
